camera_changes.env: none: wifi-ap join wrote wlanssid and wlanpass with the values they already had (sorted fw_printenv output had the same md5 before and after); no wlanap_* variable was set
camera_changes.installed_by: easy/post_setup.py version 4: --check reported 3 files to change, --reboot changed them and rebooted (back on the network about 50 s later), --check after the tests reported nothing to change
camera_changes.runtime_only: test script, test log and the test AP name and passphrase (WIFIAP_SSID and WIFIAP_PASS, environment variables of the test script only) under /tmp (tmpfs); removed after the test

gpio_source.stock_app: appfs cmsMain.out has two board tables. In the one whose IR LED GPIO matches this board (GPIO6_4, see night/README.md) the button (keystruct) is 0x80000006 = GPIO0_6 (gpio6); the other table has GPIO9_2 (gpio74)
gpio_source.stock_behaviour: the button was read every 50 ms; a press of more than 3 s switched the radio to AP mode by loading mt7601Uap.ko (log string: 3518 keydown time(%d),do cmsChangeWifiDevice2AP); each long press switched between smart config and AP mode
gpio_source.pin_mux: the stock pin table sets 0x200F0138 (GPIO0_6) to 0 = GPIO; OpenIPC boots with 1, so wifi-ap button writes 0

implementation.button: S97wifiap starts 'wifi-ap button', which reads gpio6 every 0.2 s. A press of 3-30 s, counted when it is released, switches between Wi-Fi client and AP. The idle level is learned at start and learned again after 1 min at one level
implementation.ap: wpa_supplicant and udhcpc stopped, mt7601sta unloaded, mt7601Uap.ko loaded, ra0 192.168.4.1/24, BusyBox udhcpd 192.168.4.100-150, WPA2-PSK, channel 6, SSID OpenIPC-<last 4 hex digits of the MAC>, passphrase = wlanpass unless wlanap_pass is set
implementation.back_to_client: button again, wifi-ap stop, wifi-ap join SSID PASS (saved with fw_setenv; back to AP if there is no lease in 60 s), 600 s without traffic (wlanap_idle) or a reboot
implementation.driver: the stock mt7601Uap.ko is built for the stock kernel and does not load on OpenIPC. The AP part of github.com/openipc/mt7601u (commit 0ac46553, the source of the OpenIPC station driver) was built as an AP-only module for the OpenIPC hi3518ev100 kernel with wifi/ap/build-mt7601Uap.sh (downloads pinned by commit and sha256; two builds in different directories were byte-identical)

method: post_setup.py version 4 installed the files and rebooted. The AP was started with 'wifi-ap do-press' (what the button watcher runs after a valid press) using a test SSID and passphrase. A Linux host joined it with NetworkManager, then ran wifi-ap join over SSH with the router SSID and passphrase read by fw_printenv on the camera (they never went to the host). A second cycle used wifi-ap start and wifi-ap stop with no client. The press timing was checked earlier the same day with WIFIAP_SYS pointing the watcher at a fake sysfs GPIO directory under /tmp

results.watcher_cpu: about 1.7 % (8 s in the first 8 min after the reboot)

button_logic_fake_gpio.setup: wifi-ap before the udhcpd fix, driver from the same source, WIFIAP_IDLE=40
button_logic_fake_gpio.no_traffic_40_s: client again, lease 14 s after the AP stopped
button_logic_fake_gpio.level_1_for_1_min: taken as the new idle level

bug_fixed: BusyBox 1.36.1 udhcpd on the camera did not write its pid to the pidfile named in its config. The first wifi-ap stopped udhcpd by that pid, so every AP stop left one udhcpd running (3 on unit 2; they were stopped). wifi-ap now starts udhcpd with -f in the background and keeps the pid itself; tests/test_wifi_ap.py checks that udhcpd and the traffic monitor are gone after stop
known_issues: iwconfig ra0 ends with Segmentation fault with the AP driver (no kernel oops, the AP keeps working); wifi-ap status shows the AP state instead
while the camera is an AP it cannot be reached through the router
incident: while checking the udhcpd pidfile behaviour, busybox udhcpd was once started without a config file and ran for 1-2 min with its defaults (eth0) until it was stopped. eth0 is not wired on this board, so it could not hand out addresses to anything
